role: kick (inside mic) — LF thump + beater body. Aja: TIGHT + ROUND + deep, clean attack (not boomy, not dark).
rationale: Aja kick is tight, round, deep, with a clean (not boxy, not dark) attack. HPF 30 + a -2.5 dB 31.5 Hz bell tame the sub-rumble shelf, keeping the ~58-63 Hz fundamental; -2.5 @350 de-boxes for a clean low-mid; a small +1.5 @3.5k gives the beater click definition (Aja has a defined kick, more than the dark Bonham recipe but cleaner than a modern click). API New(FF) 3:1 Medium is GENTLE density that preserves dynamics; lf +1 @60 round weight, 550 top kept flat. declick off (percussive). Polarity left as the phase-align set it.

role: kick beater / click mic — owns attack. Aja: clean defined click, sits under the 'in' mic.
rationale: HPF 90 hands the thump back to the 'in' mic; -2.5 at 200/340 kill cardboard box; +2 @3.5k presents a CLEAN beater click (below the 5-7k harsh zone); -2 @6.5k + a gentle 5-7k de-harsh keep it smooth (Aja is never harsh). 550 top flat. No transient/excite (preserve natural dynamics). declick off.

role: snare top — THE STAR of the Purdie shuffle: full round woody body + crisp-but-smooth ghost notes. Keep the dynamics; do NOT gate.
rationale: Body-dominant (peak ~200 Hz). Aja keeps the full round body: a small -1.5 @300 de-boxes without thinning; +1.5 @5k gives a CLEAN crack/presence (Aja snare is detailed), with a 4-7k dynamic de-harsh that ducks ring only when it rings so the smooth top + ghost notes survive. CRITICAL: NO gate, NO transient snap — the loud-backbeat/whisper-ghost-note dynamic contrast IS the Purdie shuffle, so the API comp ratio is kept LOW (2:1, high threshold -12) to LEVEL gently, not crush. 550 top flat. declick off; polarity left from phase-align.

role: snare bottom (wires) — buzz/snap detail. Aja: a clean touch of wires + ghost-note snap under the top.
rationale: Wires mic: HPF 150 kills shell-ring/box LF junk; -4/-2.5 @200/400 de-box; +2 @7k (ABOVE the 5 kHz harsh edge) presents a CLEAN wire buzz / ghost-note snap, with a 5-7k de-harsh guarding the edge. Sits under the snare top — a clean hint of wires that helps the ghost notes read. Comp ratio kept low (2.5:1) to keep the snap dynamics. 550 top flat. declick off.

role: hi-hat (close mic) — the shuffle's triplet hat: PRESENT + smooth + detailed (audible but never splashy/harsh).
rationale: Aja change vs the dark Bonham/TNK recipes: the hat is PRESENT + detailed (the triplet shuffle hat is a defining rhythmic element), but SMOOTH. HPF 110 kills 63-80 Hz rumble/spill; -4 @200 (whoosh/spill) + -2.5 @400 clear the box; a gentle +1 @9k lift adds sizzle DETAIL (per the salt-shaker rule: lift 8-16k, de-whoosh 160-500), while the 5-7k de-harsh tames the brittle poke. Modest lift only (the kit has a noise floor — a broad bright shelf would raise hiss). 550 top flat. declick off.

role: overheads (stereo) — clean detailed cymbal + whole-kit image. Aja: warm-but-DETAILED, smooth silky top.
rationale: The OH carries the clean, detailed kit image in a studio mix. HPF 120 dumps the worst 63-80 Hz kick lump; a gentle -1.5 @200 eases the box WITHOUT thinning the low-mid warmth; a modest +1 dB 11 kHz high-shelf adds the silky DETAIL Aja is known for (the one famous-drum recipe that ALLOWS gentle air — Bonham/TNK forbid it), guarded by a 3.15-6.3k dynamic de-harsh so it stays SMOOTH, never harsh. Old(FB) 2:1 Medium for cohesion that keeps the cymbal dynamics; 550 top flat (the corrective shelf + the bus Pultec own the air).

role: room/ambience (stereo) — TASTEFUL controlled depth (NOT the star, unlike Bonham). Clean, gives dimension.
rationale: Aja inversion vs Bonham: the room is NOT the star here — it adds tasteful, CONTROLLED depth/dimension, sitting well under the close mics. HPF 60 (tighter than Bonham's 45) + a -2 @210 + a -1 @200 in the API EQ keep the room low buildup TIGHT (Aja is controlled, not boomy); a 2.5-6k de-harsh keeps it smooth. Old(FB) 2:1 Medium at 0.3 s for gentle character WITHOUT crushing (keep the natural dynamics). declick off; polarity left from phase-align.
